novelty.justification: The claim’s core novelty is the mechanism hypothesis that jailbreaks leave harm evidence “legibly present at earlier positions” while “disrupting routing/aggregation” into the final-position refusal read-out, together with position-wise pooling as the associated measurement. Searches around “jailbreak distributed harm signal prompt token positions,” “refusal direction final token activation,” “harm representation read-out routing failure,” and “position-wise residual stream jailbreak detection” found Arditi et al.’s single refusal-direction account, AlignTree’s activation monitoring, SafeSeek’s circuit localization, and LatentBiopsy’s dissociation between harmful-intent geometry and refusal, but none posits preserved harm at content-token positions coupled to attack-induced failure of routing into the final decision position. Moving from those works to this claim requires a new core positional-routing relationship rather than merely changing the model or renaming a standard probe, although max/top-k pooling itself is a natural adaptation rather than a new general measurement paradigm; this supports high novelty within an established mechanistic-safety framework.
